# S&P / Macro Vector — Phase 0 baseline scorecard

*Generated by `scripts/spvector_baseline.py`. The dumb-baseline gate: every later candidate signal must beat these net-of-cost, out-of-sample, on Sharpe AND MaxDD.*

Allocation is long/flat (alloc in [0,1]), acts next-bar (no look-ahead). The flat sleeve earns the prevailing 3-mo T-bill yield (DTB3); `CAGR(no carry)` strips it so the rate-regime-dependent carry is transparent. Buy & hold stays all-equity.

> ⚠️ `_GSPC` (^GSPC) is a PRICE index — no dividends. Buy & hold here understates total return by ~2-4%/yr while the switch's cash sleeve earns REAL bill carry, so the apparent CAGR-beat is a dividend-omission artifact. Use `_GSPC` for DRAWDOWN, episode-counting and Sharpe-SHAPE only; the honest CAGR benchmark is SPY (total-return).

## After-tax sensitivity (taxable account, SPY 200dma switch)

At a 35% short-term rate, the 200dma switch nets **4.98% after-tax CAGR (5.07× wealth)** vs buy & hold **10.81% (30.68×)** — buy & hold defers all equity tax. Cumulative tax paid ≈ 3.31× initial capital. _Approximate model — a sensitivity, not the gate._

## Honest-N — independent bear episodes (the true sample size for a switch)

| index | history | ≥20% bears | ≥15% bears |
|---|---|--:|--:|
| SPY | 1993-01-29-2026-06-12 | 4 | 7 |
| _DJI | 1992-01-02-2026-06-12 | 4 | 7 |
| _RUT | 1987-09-10-2026-06-12 | 9 | 10 |
| _GSPC | 1927-12-30-2026-06-12 | 12 | 16 |

_The episode count — not the row count — governs overfitting: a get-out/get-back-in switch gets one near-binary draw per bear. SPY's ~4 independent ≥20% bears is why any single-config CAGR beat is suspect; ^GSPC (_GSPC) to 1927 lifts the count to the only level that materially moves confidence._
